Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and the visual-signal inspection skill before proposing or editing the policy. I’ll keep the candidate reasoning and reusable guidance separate as requested.

The contract confirms that the candidate must remain materializable throughout and that CFD is deferred. I’m now anchoring the two visual views to scores, trajectory metrics, diagnostics, inherited guidance, and the current prefilled policy; only after that will I read the bookshelf mechanisms.

All sampled sheets satisfy direct uniform still-water initialization. The best and worst sampled captures—and the distinct-policy sample—show the same self-propelled, target-bending alternating top-down street and compact caudal 3D structures; there is no visual failure class among these four. I’m checking detailed route, actuation, and load statistics next so the proposed ablation is tied to the robustness evidence rather than tiny score spread.

The sampled distinct variant only adds a rearward route boost, yet lands inside the same capture class; the other three are executable-identical replications. The inherited lesson therefore points to a clean removal of the disputed half-cycle relief redistribution, not another stacked route channel. Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m now consulting the primitive and source references; adoption remains contingent on whether any invariant addresses this specific robustness boundary.

The bookshelf did not justify a new primitive: the existing controller already implements the transferable target-signed curvature and joint-state half-cycle steering invariants. It instead reinforced preserving those mechanisms while making one evidence-led ablation—remove only common-envelope relief redistribution, whose identical executable has both captures and inherited misses. I’ll record that diagnosis and falsification boundary before touching the candidate.

The single candidate is now a clean architecture ablation: it removes the redistribution parameter and logic while leaving the target curvature, displacement-only steering, response release, propulsion, and projection unchanged. I also revised the durable lesson: a capture cannot validate a recovery channel that never meaningfully activates, and score-only inherited logs cannot establish that attribution. Next I’m running the mandated contract checker and targeted static checks—no CFD.

The checker specification is itself a three-part non-CFD validation. I’m invoking the configured check-runner now; it will verify the semantic guidance delta, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary guard.

A useful inherited artifact surfaced during static inspection: the parent optimizer log contains an executable geometry-scheduled policy with no redistribution—the same mechanism as this ablation—and a completed capture score. I’m checking executable equivalence and its full metrics/views now; if confirmed, I’ll strengthen the notes and durable lesson with that prior evidence while still treating this worker’s own CFD as unevaluated.

The checker found one manifest-level issue and one environment limitation: the rendered README marks the same parent twice, so the guidance checker counts two parents; the boundary guard passes, while Julia is absent from `PATH`. I’ll first fold the newly confirmed inherited clean-ablation capture into the evidence files, then repair the duplicate parent marker minimally and search for an available local Julia runtime before rerunning checks.

The inherited parent log confirms executable equivalence (comments only differ) and supplies completed positive evidence: direct-uniform capture at `18.6395T`, mean distance `2.09383L`, with the same coherent top-down and oblique wake class. It does not prove robustness or demand relief—acceleration contact remains `60.81%/73.12%` and rate contact `11.09%/15.05%`—so this candidate is an intentional independent replication of the clean ablation, not a claimed new gain improvement. I’m updating both evidence records accordingly.

The duplicate marker was the same parent entry repeated verbatim in the rendered README; I removed only the duplicate so the checker can identify the assigned parent. A local Julia 1.12.6 runtime exists outside `PATH`, so I’ll rerun the same contract command with that runtime prepended, then rerun all three checks through the configured runner.

All mandated checks now pass: material guidance/notes update, Julia policy contract and finite two-joint action, and solver editable-boundary guard. I’m doing one final non-CFD handoff audit for non-empty files and the exact policy delta, then I’ll return the candidate paths and evidence boundary.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1).

- Cleanly removes phase-dependent amplitude-relief redistribution while preserving target-signed curvature, displacement-only half-cycle steering, response release, posterior lag, and acceleration projection.
- Updated [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) with visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, inherited capture evidence, and falsification criteria.
- Materially revised [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:1).
- Guidance, Julia contract, and solver-boundary checks pass.
- Removed a duplicated parent marker in `README.md` that initially prevented guidance validation.
- No CFD was run; evaluation remains deferred to EvE.
